minutes.headline: Water commissioners approved the annual town meeting warrant and discussed replacing the engineering firm.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners approved the minutes and voted to accept the articles for the annual meeting. They discussed a pump replacement at well 5, a pilot study for manganese and PFAS treatment at the Hickory Hills well, and a new work truck. They also discussed dropping their current engineering firm and replacing mains with the water enhancement money.

votes.motion: Accept the articles for the annual meeting

budget_items.what_was_said: Article five appropriates money into an account for water main replacement and maintenance.
Article six is for a new vehicle and will need modification after discussion.
Article seven covers new software and moving the SCADA control panel to the new office.
Article eight funds repair or replacement of the pump at pumping station number five, in service since 1985.

Article nine takes money from the water enhancement account for an engineer to run a pilot study on treating manganese and PFAS. A cheaper short test was rejected in favor of the full long-term pilot.

The quote came in above the article amount; dropping the full plow setup and some options brings it close to the article figure. Leftover vehicle money stays in the district's account, and trade-in value was mentioned.
The estimate was originally lower and is probably higher now. The superintendent wants to apply for state revolving fund money.
Pipe prices are rising and the money in the article is for water main work. Plastic pipe has more than doubled per foot.

decisions.decision: The superintendent will research engineering consultants and come back with recommendations. The current firm may be invited to explain its delays.
Engineering consultants will be listed as an old business item.
The board will decline the offered swampy parcel on Reservoir Road.
A meeting with the Weston and Sampson engineer is to be set for the 23rd, earlier in the day, before the annual meeting on the 26th.
Leaning toward replacing Lancaster Ave and Rolling Acres mains with in-house work this summer, in phases.

what_happened.line: Commissioners voted unanimously to accept the articles for the annual town meeting warrant.
The superintendent will research replacement engineering consultants; the current firm may be asked to explain its delays.
The board plans to decline an offered swampy parcel on Reservoir Road.
Commissioners are leaning toward replacing the Lancaster Ave and Rolling Acres mains with in-house work this summer, in phases.
The truck quote came in above the article amount; dropping the plow setup and some options would bring it close.

why_it_matters: The warrant articles, including a well pump, a manganese and PFAS pilot study, a vehicle and main replacement, are what water district voters will be asked to approve at the annual meeting.
Rising pipe prices and a possible change of engineering firm bear on how far the main replacement money goes and how quickly the Hickory Hills treatment work moves.
